studies.label: Classroom experiment: randomized AI adoption or discontinuation during the future-idea upgrade task

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.1, analyzed sample
counts_source.quote: 분석에 포함된 참여자는 총 164명이며, 1차 조건은 A 83 명, B 81명으로 구성되었다. 2차 조건은 A1 43명, A2 40명, B1 41명, B2 40명이다.

arms.name: A1 (maintain AI)
arms.description: Generative AI available in the initial draft and maintained for the upgrade; randomized within initial group A.

arms.name: A2 (discontinue AI)
arms.description: Generative AI available in the initial draft and removed for the upgrade; randomized within initial group A. The generative_ai code records prior exposure; the scored upgrade was produced without AI.

arms.name: B1 (adopt AI)
arms.description: Initial draft produced without AI; generative AI introduced for the upgrade, randomized within initial group B.

arms.name: B2 (maintain no AI)
arms.description: No AI in either the initial draft or the upgrade; randomized within initial group B.

studies.task: Students generated up to 10 ideas for improving life in 2035 during a 10-minute initial round, then revised, supplemented, or elaborated their own ideas for 10 minutes after an approximately 30-minute break in the same session (PDF p. 5, printed p. 44, Section 3.1).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (Free plan; version available by default at the time), with other generative AI tools also permitted
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.1, continuation of step (1); no underlying model version or release year specified

estimates.outcome: Gain in total creativity score from initial draft to upgrade (H3)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two independent raters, blind to condition, scored each idea on novelty, usefulness/feasibility, elaboration/specificity, and future-change fit. Idea scores range from 0 to 10; scores for up to 10 ideas are summed to a participant total ranging from 0 to 100, and the two raters' totals are averaged. Similar or duplicate ideas within a participant's round receive novelty deductions. The analyzed outcome here is the participant's round-2 total minus round-1 total. The total combines idea quantity and quality. Rater expertise is not stated, so human_raters is provisional. Scoring: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Sections 3.2.3-3.2.4.

stats.difference_is: Treatment minus control in mean gain (each gain is round-2 total minus round-1 total)

regression.model: Planned contrast of time-by-condition effects from the linear mixed-effects model score ~ time * round_2_group + (1 | participant), with A1 as the reference condition. The model includes all analyzed participants; the contrast compares the two arms within one initial-group randomization stratum. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 3.3.4.

estimates.notes: AI adoption during the upgrade versus continued non-use. Both arms produced their initial draft without AI. All statistics refer to gains; the reported positive contrast is B1 gain minus B2 gain. This is a paper-designated main planned contrast (PDF p. 6, printed p. 45, Section 3.3.4), but no preregistration is reported. SDs describe participant-level change scores, not individual ideas or separate ratings. No days-long follow-up is reported; both rounds were in the same session. The model accounts for within-participant repeated measurements with a random intercept.

sources.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 47), Section 4.4.2, H4 planned contrast

estimates.notes: AI maintained during the upgrade versus AI withdrawn. Both arms produced their initial draft with AI. The paper calls this the discontinuation effect but defines it as A1 gain minus A2 gain, so the printed positive sign is retained. This is a paper-designated main planned contrast (PDF p. 6, printed p. 45, Section 3.3.4), but no preregistration is reported. SDs describe participant-level change scores, not individual ideas or separate ratings. No days-long follow-up is reported; both rounds were in the same session. The model accounts for within-participant repeated measurements with a random intercept.

not_extracted.what: S2-O1: Round-1 total creativity, A (AI access) versus B (no AI), H1
not_extracted.reason: The paper does not state how the initial A/B allocation was made. Randomization is stated only for the subsequent split within each initial group, so this contrast is not established as randomized. PDF pp. 4-5 (printed pp. 43-44), Section 3.1; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 4.2.

not_extracted.what: S2-O2: Unassisted round-2 total creativity after AI discontinuation, A2 versus B2
not_extracted.reason: This comparison crosses the initial A/B allocation, whose randomization is not stated. The paper supplies arm descriptions and descriptive scores but no direct test of this after_ai contrast. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.1; PDF p. 7 (printed p. 46), Table 4.

not_extracted.what: H2: Overall round-1-to-round-2 improvement, pooled across conditions
not_extracted.reason: A pooled before/after repetition effect with mixed AI exposure, without an AI-versus-comparison contrast. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 46), Section 4.3 and Table 2.

not_extracted.what: Within-arm paired changes for A1, A2, B1, and B2, including the A1 reference-group time coefficient
not_extracted.reason: These compare each arm with its own earlier performance. They do not isolate randomized AI assistance, and condition order was not randomized. Their paired t tests, within-arm confidence intervals, and dz values must not be attached to the between-arm gain contrasts. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 46), Table 3 and Section 4.4.2.

not_extracted.what: H5: Switching asymmetry, (B1 gain minus B2 gain) minus (A1 gain minus A2 gain)
not_extracted.reason: An interaction comparing the two extracted treatment effects across initial AI histories, rather than an additional contrast between two randomized arms. Initial AI history was not established as randomly assigned. PDF p. 8 (printed p. 47), Section 4.4.2, item 3.

not_extracted.what: Round-1 homogeneity checks, A1 versus A2 and B1 versus B2
not_extracted.reason: Baseline balance checks before the randomized round-2 AI manipulation; both arms in each check had the same AI access when the baseline output was produced. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 3.3.1 and Table 1.
Only overall idea counts by round are reported; there are no arm-level fluency statistics or AI contrasts. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.2.2.

not_extracted.what: Separate novelty, usefulness/feasibility, elaboration/specificity, and future-change-fit scores
not_extracted.reason: The dimensions contribute to the extracted total, but arm-level dimension outcomes and contrasts are not reported. The reported dimension-specific ICCs measure rater reliability rather than AI effects. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.2.1; PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 3.2.4.

open_items: Initial assignment to A versus B is not described as random. The screening form's S2 comparisons remain ineligible unless that allocation can be confirmed.

The number assigned and the number excluded are not printed. Only students who completed both rounds were analyzed, so n_randomized remains null for the study and arms (PDF p. 5, printed p. 44, Section 3.1).
The background of the two independent raters is not stated; human_raters is provisional rather than a confirmed lay-rater classification (PDF p. 6, printed p. 45, Section 3.2.4).
The exact ChatGPT model, its release year, and which alternative generative AI tools were actually used are not reported; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF p. 5, printed p. 44, Section 3.1).
The paper does not report arm-level idea counts, mean quality per idea, or separate rubric-dimension effects, so quantity and quality cannot be separated from the total.
No preregistration, supplementary appendix, or posted-data location is stated in the document.
notes: Read the complete markdown conversion, including references and author biographies; the document contains no appendix. Every cited PDF page was checked with pymupdf, and Table 4 was also recovered with find_tables. Only the randomized comparisons within initial groups enter estimates. The screening form's S1 and S2 refer to the same students, not separate samples; S2 is listed in not_extracted. Each extracted contrast uses the entire relevant randomization stratum, rather than a post hoc subgroup. n_total records that stratum's printed participant count; the mixed model is fitted to the full study sample. The study repeats measurement within participants but randomizes the upgrade condition between participants; within_person is null because these are between-arm gain contrasts, not crossover paired-condition estimates. The extracted means and SDs are change scores from Table 4, not round-2 score levels. The main model reports planned contrasts of gains; Table 4's separate round-level columns are not substituted for gain-score statistics. The same printed planned-contrast estimate and SE are retained as both difference fields and regression fields; these are not separate analyses. The paper prints no standardized between-arm effect for these contrasts. se_basis is participant because the model contains a participant random intercept; no robust or cluster-sandwich SE estimator is specified, so regression.se_type is not_stated. Both effects answer with_ai because the treatment arm had AI during the scored upgrade; A2's prior AI use does not turn the A1-versus-A2 comparison into after_ai. The paper explicitly describes an experiment in actual coursework, supporting field_rct. South Korea is inferred from the Korean paper's reference to domestic universities. No cross-person diversity outcome is measured. No cross-paper sample overlap is identified in the screening form.
